ports.name: o_done
ports.behaviour_evidence: probe RUN #2 (o_done=1 at t=5, t=125, t=245; 0 at t=15..115, t=135..235, t=255); RTL 'assign o_done = (round_ff == 4\'d0);'
ports.function: Result valid; high for one cycle when o_data holds the plaintext.
ports.note: In the RTL o_done is combinational (= round_ff==0) and is high right after reset (t=5 in probe RUN #2), before any start; the architecture expects o_done=0 after reset and only high at the end of an operation, and marks it as registered. See assumptions H1 and H2.

ports.name: o_data
ports.behaviour_evidence: testbench lines 57-62 (o_data compared to 128'h3243f6a8885a308d313198a2e0370734); probe RUN #2 (observed output 00000000000000600000000000000000 and 00000000000000970000000000000000 at the two o_done pulses, both FAIL)
ports.function: 128-bit plaintext block; correct plaintext in the row where o_done=1.
ports.note: In the RTL o_data is combinational from current_data_ff (a register); the architecture marks it as registered. Functionally similar (holds the plaintext when o_done=1). See assumption H2.

clock_and_reset.clock: clk (1 bit, positive edge, period 10 time units)
clock_and_reset.evidence: rtl_structure.json (async_reset: rst_async_n, reset_level: low, clock_edge: pos for round_ff and current_data_ff); testbench lines 76-80 (rst_async_n=1, #1, rst_async_n=0, #2, rst_async_n=1); probe RUN #2 (samples at rising edges of clk)

assumptions.subject: o_done
assumptions.statement: o_done is high right after reset (t=5 in probe RUN #2), before any start, because the RTL computes o_done = (round_ff == 0) and round_ff resets to 0. The architecture's schedule expects o_done=0 after reset and only high at the end of an operation. Whether the post-reset high level is intended or a fault is not determined in this order (ALIGN-INTERFACE, not fault-finding).

assumptions.subject: o_done, o_data
assumptions.statement: In the RTL o_done and o_data are combinational (o_done = round_ff==0; o_data = current_data_ff), while the architecture marks both as registered. The functional behaviour (one-cycle pulse for o_done; plaintext held when o_done=1 for o_data) is the same, but the implementation (combinational vs registered) differs.

assumptions.subject: i_update_key
assumptions.statement: i_update_key is x (undefined) from t=0 to t=20 in the testbench because the initial block does not drive it (only i_start=0 is set); it becomes defined only when Simple_test assigns it. The architecture assumes i_update_key=0 in all rows after the start row.
